jurisdiction.name: Financial Stability Board
jurisdiction.overview: Official documents of this organisation are listed on its own page and are not counted in member countries' totals.

narrative.summary: The FSB has examined AI in finance since its 2017 report on AI and machine learning in financial services, followed by reports to the G20 on the financial stability implications of AI (2024) and on monitoring AI adoption (2025). In October 2026 it finalised 12 non-binding Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of AI by financial institutions, covering organisation-wide AI governance and lifecycle risk management.
lead_institutions: FSB Standing Committee on Assessment of Vulnerabilities

instruments.official_title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning in financial services: Market developments and financial stability implications
instruments.english_title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning in financial services
instruments.summary: First FSB assessment of how AI and machine learning are used in financial services (credit scoring, insurance pricing, trading, fraud detection, supervision) and of their financial stability implications. It identifies benefits and risks, including new interconnections from shared data, reliance on a few third-party providers, and models that are hard to interpret or audit, and stresses testing, monitoring and governance as adoption grows.
instruments.current_status: Report published by the Financial Stability Board on 1 November 2017.
instruments.evidence_reference: Date and PDF from the FSB publication page. The 2024 report states it revisits this one. Classed as an FSB report (published as an FSB document); kept as record per brief rule that FSB reports count. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, 1 Nov 2017 date and summary content confirmed.; 'FSB reports are not legally binding' is not stated on the source.

instruments.official_title: The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.english_title: The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: Reviews AI adoption in finance since 2017, including generative AI, and identifies AI-related vulnerabilities that could raise systemic risk: third-party dependencies and provider concentration, correlated market behaviour, cyber risk, and model, data and governance risk. It concludes existing frameworks cover many risks and calls on authorities to close data gaps, assess whether policy frameworks are adequate, and strengthen supervisory capacity, including with AI tools.
instruments.current_status: Published by the Financial Stability Board on 14 November 2024 and listed by the FSB among its reports to the G20. Not legally binding.
instruments.evidence_reference: Date from FSB publication page and press release R14112024. Page tags it under content type 'Reports to the G20'; no explicit endorsement statement found, so current_status says only 'listed among reports to the G20'.

instruments.official_title: Monitoring Adoption of Artificial Intelligence and Related Vulnerabilities in the Financial Sector
instruments.english_title: Monitoring Adoption of Artificial Intelligence and Related Vulnerabilities in the Financial Sector
instruments.summary: Sets out indicators and approaches for financial authorities to monitor AI adoption and related vulnerabilities. It recommends that national authorities apply the indicators, formalise metrics with domestic partners, deepen engagement with firms, explore AI tools for monitoring and share data across regulators, and that the FSB and standard-setting bodies support cross-border information exchange and more consistent taxonomies.
instruments.current_status: Published by the Financial Stability Board on 10 October 2025, prepared at the request of the South African G20 Presidency. Not legally binding.
instruments.evidence_reference: Cover date 10 October 2025 read from the PDF; PDF states it was prepared at the request of the South African G20 Presidency. HTML landing page not fetched; PDF is on fsb.org.

instruments.official_title: Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI): Final report
instruments.english_title: Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
instruments.summary: Sets out 12 sound practices that financial institutions are encouraged to consider when adopting AI, in two groups: organisation-wide AI governance (board and senior management alignment with strategy and risk appetite, roles and responsibilities, integrating AI risk into risk frameworks, adaptive oversight) and lifecycle risk management (materiality assessment, technology choice, data governance, explainability, performance evaluation, human oversight, cyber and ICT risk, third-party AI dependencies).
instruments.current_status: Final report published by the Financial Stability Board on 15 October 2026 after public consultation. The FSB states the practices are non-prescriptive and do not form a binding international standard.
instruments.evidence_reference: Cover date 15 October 2026 read from PDF; non-binding wording from PDF. Consultation version cover date 10 June 2026, deadline 22 July 2026, read from P100626.pdf. Page classes it under 'Reports to the G20' but no endorsement statement found.
